answers.towns_excluded:
Just a caution about of error here:
All of those towns are in Polk County, FL. Every one of the 20 places on your list (the 12 confirmed, the 7 website-only, and Lakeland Highlands) sits inside Polk County. So you can keep the whole list and Polk County stays the main location entity.

There’s a bonus here. Polk County has exactly the same boundaries as the Lakeland–Winter Haven, FL MSA. That means the county entity and the MSA entity cover the same area, and you can use either one as the wrapper without leaving any town out.

Two things to watch for:

Davenport and Haines City mailing addresses. The Davenport ZIP codes (and a bit of Haines City’s) extend into the Four Corners area, which is in Osceola, Lake and Orange counties. The cities themselves are in Polk. But if the client starts naming developments like ChampionsGate or Four Corners, those would be outside the county.
Unincorporated places. Highland City, Kathleen, Wahneta, Waverly and Lakeland Highlands are unincorporated communities (census-designated places), not cities. They’re fine to list in areas served, but they’re weaker entities than the incorporated cities. I’d keep them in the list rather than giving them their own location pages.
